additional_concerns: For node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909, preserved processing of a pending application becomes a substantive relief exclusion. The source expressly preserves the existing process but does not expressly establish that broader disqualification. Retain this as a proposed interpretation, including uncertainty about subsequent decisions, withdrawal and resubmission.

Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from scope rather than deciding their relief eligibility. That matches its narrower question but cannot resolve the transition for excluded applications.

The introductory immediate-effect statement and the specific 28 November 2025 commencement provision require reconciliation. The specific implementation provision supports the chosen date, but the legally relevant assessment event and any universal implementation-date test are not established.

The relevant updated UCITS FAQs and existing approval or authorisation rules are missing authorities for resolving actual procedural availability and the transition. The supplied dependency IDs have null source_hash values and no descriptive mapping; neither can safely be assigned to a particular missing authority.

Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and authoritative guidance on novel or complex features and possible local policy implications are needed to determine the supplied classifications in an actual case. The formulas accept these judgments as inputs rather than establishing them.

Node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 has no executable formalization. Its separation of substantive qualification from preserved processing retains an unresolved interpretation; it supplies no executable answer about actual relief.
Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa deliberately tests substantive conditions only. Its positive result cannot establish permission to bypass preserved application processing.

The descriptive supervision aim does not expressly impose an additional item (ii) eligibility condition. Importing the express supervision condition from item (i) would require further support. Conversely, these scoped assessments do not establish that supervision can never matter under the missing FAQs.
